caseno: Appeal from original Order No. 96 of 1974 with Civil Rule No. 1054 (S.M.) of 1974.
lawyer:
A.H.M. Sadat Ali Khan ----- For the Appellants.
Ahmad Sobhan and Md. Ruhul Amin ----- For Respondents 1 & 2.
parties:
Aktamunnessa and anr. ----- Pre-emptors-Appellants.
Vs.
Habibullah and others ----- Pre-emptors-Respondents.
full_judgment:
The preemptors Habibullah and Rustam Ali filed an application under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act XXVIII of 1951) for preempting 2.98 acres of land of plot No. 1602 and .08 acre of land of plot No. 1605 of khatian No. 294 of Mouza Tamta, P.S. Ramganj, District Noakhali. By a registered kabala dated 28.8.69 opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 sold .34 acres of land in plot No. 1594 .07 acre of land in plot No. 1596 .39 acre of land in plot No. 1601, 2.98 acres of land in plot No. 1602 and .08 acre of land in plot No. 1605 of C.S. khatian No. 294 of Mouza Tamta, P. S. Ramganj, to the stranger-purchasers defendant opposite parties 1 and 2 for a sum of Tk. 15,000/00. The kabala was registered on 25.9.69. The petitioners are contiguous owners of land of plots No. 1602 and No. 1605. The petitioners paid the proportionate value of land, that is, Tk. 11,895/00 as well as the usual compensation. The petition for preemption was fixed on 13.1.70. 

 4. Mr. Sadat Ali Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners mainly argues that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an illegality by allowing partial preemption of two plots of land out of five plots of one khatian and also argues that the application under section 96 of the said Act is not in proper form. 

 In section 2(13) of the said Act the term 'holding' has been defined to mean a parcel or parcels of land or an undivided share thereof, held by a raiyat or an under raiyat and forming the subject of a separate tenancy. It is undisputed that partial preemption of a holding or a share thereof which has been transferred is not permitted in law. The preemptor must preempt the entire land of the holding or portion thereof which has been transferred. In the instant case .34 acre of land in plot No. 1594, '07 acre of land in plot No. 1596-39 acre of land in plot No. 1601, 2.98 acres of land in plot No. 1602 and .608 acre of land in plot No. 1605 of khatian No. 294 belonged to one holding and the said plots comprising 3.87 acres of land were transferred under the disputed kabala. The preemptors deposited the proportionate price of land and the usual compensation for only two plots, that is plots No. 1602 and No. 1605 being the contiguous owner of land of these two plots. This apparently they did under a misapprehension of law that they are not entitled to preempt other plots of land of which they are not contiguous owners. We have already stated that they are entitled to preempt the entire area of the holding which has been transferred under the kabala if he is a contiguous owner of the holding. We respectfully agree with the decision in the case of Syed Abdul Karim and others Vs. Harendra Chandra Dhupi and others in 14 D.L.R. 847.
